brands.description: The Print Shop is a basic desktop publishing software package developed in the early 1980s by Brøderbund. It was unique in that it provided libraries of clip-art and templates through a simple interface to build signs, posters and banners with household dot-matrix printers. Over the years the software has been updated to accommodate changing file formats and printer technologies.
brands.name: The Print Shop

brands.description: Promotional merchandise, promotional items, promotional products, promotional gifts, or advertising gifts, sometimes nicknamed swag, are articles of merchandise (often branded with a logo or slogan) used in marketing and communication programs. They are given away to promote a company, corporate image, brand, or event at trade shows, conferences, and as part of guerrilla marketing campaigns.
brands.name: Promotional merchandise

brands.description: Print on demand (POD) is a printing technology and business process in which copies of a book (or other document) are not printed until an order has been received, allowing books to be printed singly, or in small quantities.
brands.name: Print on demand

brands.description: OneDrive (previously SkyDrive, Windows Live SkyDrive, and Windows Live Folders) is a file hosting service that allows users to sync files and later access them from a web browser or mobile device. Users can share files publicly or with their contacts; publicly shared files do not require a Microsoft account to access them.
brands.name: OneDrive

brands.description: Dropbox is a file hosting service operated by Dropbox, Inc., headquartered in San Francisco, California, that offers cloud storage, file synchronization, personal cloud, and client software.
brands.name: Dropbox (service)

brands.description: PayPal Holdings, Inc. is an American company operating a worldwide online payments system. Online money transfers serve as electronic alternatives to traditional paper methods like checks and money orders. PayPal is one of the world's largest Internet payment companies.
brands.name: PayPal

brands.description: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet developed by Microsoft for Windows, Mac OS X, and iOS. It features calculation, graphing tools, pivot tables, and a macro programming language called Visual Basic for Applications. It has been a very widely applied spreadsheet for these platforms, especially since version 5 in 1993, and it has replaced Lotus 1-2-3 as the industry standard for spreadsheets.
brands.name: Microsoft Excel

namedLocations.description: Contin (Gaelic: Cunndainn) is a Ross-shire village and civil parish between Strathpeffer and Garve in the Highland council area of Scotland. The parish has a population of 675. The church in Contin is dedicated to St Maelrubha or Máel Ruba and is on Contin Island which lies in the Black Water (Conon) and is reached from the rest of the village by two bridges, one foot and the other road.
namedLocations.name: Contin

namedLocations.description: A ZIP Code is a postal code used by the United States Postal Service (USPS) in a system it introduced in 1963. The term ZIP is an acronym for Zone Improvement Plan; it was chosen to suggest that the mail travels more efficiently and quickly (zipping along) when senders use the code in the postal address. The basic format consists of five digits. An extended ZIP+4 code was introduced in 1983 which includes the five digits of the ZIP Code, followed by a hyphen and four additional digits that reference a more specific location.
namedLocations.name: ZIP Code

namedLocations.description: Ahmedabad (/ˈəhmədɑːbɑːd/ is the largest city and former capital of the Indian state of Gujarat. It is the administrative headquarters of the Ahmadabad district and the seat of the Gujarat High Court. Ahmedabad's population of 5,633,927 (as per 2011 population census) makes it the fifth-most populous city in India, and the encompassing urban agglomeration population estimated at 6,357,693 is the seventh-most populous in India. Ahmadabad is located on the banks of the Sabarmati River, 30 km (19 mi) from the state capital Gandhinagar, which is its twin city.
namedLocations.name: Ahmedabad

namedLocations.description: A cheque (or check in American English) is a document that orders a bank to pay a specific amount of money from a person's account to the person in whose name the cheque has been issued. The person writing the cheque, the drawer, has a transaction banking account (often called a current, cheque, chequing or checking account) where their money is held.
namedLocations.name: Cheque

transcript.text: Hello and welcome back.
Welcome to Part 2 of our on Print shop version 12.2 features tutorial.
In the first part, we covered updates like configurable products in offline orders, tier based pricing, shipping enhancements and storefront usability improvements.
In this video, we'll continue exploring more powerful updates.
Each of these enhancements is designed to give you greater flexibility, efficiency and control.
Let's begin with some powerful updates in the Order module first.
Admins can now define custom formats for quote IDs and system generated order product IDs.
This means you can set patterns that align with your internal documentation or workflow standards, ensuring better organization and consistency across your business records.
Please note that you need to connect with the On Print Shop technical team to set your preferred ID pattern.
Moving ahead in the Order History tab, you'll now find a detailed Production Time Spent summary, along with a new status change column in Reports.
This gives admins clearer visibility into how long each production stage takes, making it easier to analyze bottlenecks and improve overall efficiency.
Next, reward points management has become more flexible.
Admins can now choose where the points should be credited at the time of order placement or only after order completion.
Plus, the system keeps track of pending, approved, and even cancel points, giving you more transparency and better control over loyalty programs.
Next, a new Payment request tab has been introduced under Order Actions.
Instead of juggling different workflows, admins can now create and manage all payment requests directly from this central tab, making financial operations smoother and faster.
POS payments are now more flexible.
Earlier limited to direct payment in the offline order flow, POS can now also be used at the time of payment request.
For online payment methods, admins can either mark the request as paid or click pay Now to complete the transaction through the payment gateway.
This enhancement streamlines deferred payments for offline orders, providing greater flexibility in managing in store transactions.
Next, we'll look at the new features in the admin panel.
To start with, production planning is now more transparent.
You'll see total production days and production due dates displayed in the Price and weight details section, visible only to admins.
This gives you quick access to production timelines, helping you plan better and respond faster to customer commitments.
Another big time saver is the ability to import FAQs in bulk using a structured template.
This drastically cuts down manual work, ensures consistency and helps you keep your support content updated with minimal effort.
File transfers are now much more secure with the added support for SFTP and FTPS protocols, ensuring that sensitive files can be safely exchanged across different printing environments.
With this enhancement, when the admin has set up the hot folder transfer printer wise in the Edit printer screen, the SFTP and FTPS driver test connection options will be available for branding.
The platform now supports SVG format for logo uploads.
This means your storefront logos are always crisp, scalable, and high quality, whether viewed on small mobile screens or large desktop monitors.
We've also added more flexibility for product promotion.
Admins can now select specific product IDs for homepage product blocks, making it easy to highlight seasonal offers, featured items, or products you want to push forward.
And lastly, to ensure smooth communication, a proactive e-mail alert system has been added.
Every 48 hours, the system checks for delivery failures and notifies admins via e-mail and dashboard alerts.
For the error notification, the admin can configure e-mail ID separated by a comma on the respective e-mail connection page.
This way, you can spot and fix issues before they affect your customers.
Shifting focus to the Designer Studio, this release adds several features to make the customization experience richer and more accurate.
First, admins can configure a default border width in percentage.
When enabled, any newly uploaded die cut image will automatically generate with this preset border width.
Border colour changes are now applied in real time instead of only after closing the colour picker for die cut canvas and pattern products.
Admins can now set default events for pattern products.
For example, if rotation, spacing or other options are preconfigured, uploaded images will automatically apply those settings when generating the pattern.
Next, the admin can choose whether non printable elements should be included in the final print ready file.
A new option Include non printable elements in Print Ready files has been added under Studio Settings to manage this.
When enabled, any non printable elements used in a customer's design will still appear in the Print Ready file, allowing customers to visualize their complete artwork before printing.
Moving to the next functionality, we've introduced the Enable Transparent Background setting in the Studio Settings.
When this setting is turned off, transparent areas in uploaded PDF files appear with a solid white background in the preview.
This means customers won't see the transparency effect during design review.
When the setting is turned on, the system displays transparent backgrounds accurately, allowing customers to see exactly how their final artwork will appear.

This feature applies specifically to PDF files with transparency, while non transparent files remain unaffected, and if multiple file types are uploaded, transparency will apply only to the PDF pages.
Another very useful tool is the image straightening option.
Customers can now quickly fix tilted or rotated images during customization, ensuring professional and polished results.
Finally, we've also made visualization more advanced.
3D models are now visible both on the Browse design page and in the upload center.
This gives customers a more realistic preview of the final product before placing an order.
And that brings us to the end of Part 2 of our On Print Shop Version 12.2 features tutorial.
In this video, we covered updates to the Order Module, Product section, Admin Panel, Storefront, and Designer Studio, each one designed to make your print store more powerful and user friendly.
In Part 3, we'll continue exploring the final set of enhancements included in this release.
If you have any questions, our support team is ready to help.
You can reach us via live chat or e-mail us at support at onprintshop com.
